# Expression type tables

<!-- Generated by tools/exprtables (exprtables page) from the type decisions of
     programs/blitz2/src/exprtype.c; do not edit.  After a change of the rules,
     build the target expression_type_tables_update and commit this file. -->

These tables list the type rules of an expression in `blitz2` as the compiler
applies them: for one operation of two values, the type each operand is taken
in and the type that results, for every operator, operand type and type so far.
The rules and the reasons for them are explained in
[The type of an expression in blitz2](expression-types.md); this page only
lists them. It is generated from the compiler's type decisions
(`programs/blitz2/src/exprtype.c`) by `tools/exprtables`, and the build checks
that it is up to date.

## How to read the tables

An expression is compiled from left to right with one *type so far*. It starts
as the type the expression is wanted in: the type of the destination of an
assignment or of a parameter, Long for an array index, none for `If`, `While`,
`Until` and `Print` and for the right operand of a comparison. Every value of a
higher type raises it ([The types and the "type so
far"](expression-types.md#the-types-and-the-type-so-far)).

Each table is for one operator, or for several that behave the same. A row is
an operation `a OP b` of two variables or function values of the types *left*
and *right*; a column is the type so far when the left operand is met. For the
first operation of an expression that is the wanted type; for a later operation
of a chain (the second `+` of `a+b+c`) it is the type the chain has reached,
and the left operand is the value computed so far. So the same operation can
have another type in another place of an expression: that is what makes the
result depend on the order of the operands.

A cell `L R → T` says: the left operand is taken as type L, the right one
as type R, and the operation leaves the type so far T. The letters are B Byte,
W Word, L Long, Q Quick, F Float, – none.

* An operand taken as a higher type than its own is converted up first; `↓`
  marks a Quick or Float operand converted down to a whole number (a Quick
  rounded down, a Float truncated towards zero).
* `Q~` is a Quick that keeps its fraction under a Long type so far: the operation
  is computed exactly and its result rounded to a whole number at the operator
  (#1178).
  The operators `&`, `|`, `AND`, `OR`, `EOR`, `LSL`, `ASL`, `LSR`, `ASR`, `Mod`, `BitTst`, `BitSet`, `BitClr`, `BitChg` take it rounded
  down (`L↓`), as the original does.
* `illegal`: the compiler refuses the operation ("Illegal Operator for Type").
* † marks a cell that differs when the operands are swapped (listed below
  each table).

The value of the whole expression is converted to the wanted type at the end;
that conversion is not part of the tables. A constant is fetched by its own
rule ("Constants", below), so an operation with a constant operand follows
the row of the type the constant takes. String operands (`+` and the
comparisons take them) are not shown.

Under a Quick type so far (#1209) a Quick operand of these operators is made a
whole number first (rounded down, its fraction bits cleared), and the result is
a Quick: `q AND p` with `q=1.5` and `p=2.5` is 0. A Float has none of them.

## Shifts

The right operand is the count. A shift of a Quick works on its 16.16 value, so
the fraction takes part (`x LSR 1` with `x=5` is 2.5).

## Comparisons

A comparison leaves a Word, its boolean (-1 or 0), as the type so far. Its
operands are compared with their own values (#1177): the right operand starts
with no type so far, a left operand that is one element (a variable, field,
array element or function value) keeps its own type, and the lower of the
two is converted up to the other. A Long and a Quick (`L Q`, `Q L`) are compared exactly:
the Long against the whole part of the Quick, on equality the fraction decides;
the Long is not converted to a Quick.

The cells marked † differ from the comparison with its operands swapped and mirrored (`b>a` for `a<b`, `b=a` for `a=b`). Each pair, the swapped one written in its own order:

* left B, right Q, type so far L: `L Q → W`; swapped: `Q Q → W`
* left W, right Q, type so far L: `L Q → W`; swapped: `Q Q → W`

A left operand that is itself an operation (`q*2`, `q+q`) is not one element: it
is computed in the type so far, as the left operand of any operator, and only
then compared (#1183, open): `r.l=(q*2>2.4)` with `q=1.25` is 0, as 2.5 is
rounded down to 2 under the Long.

An `=` and `<>` comparison of one Byte value with one constant from 128 to 255
takes the constant as the byte it stands for, sign-extended as the Byte is
(#978): `a.b=$90 : If a=$90` is true.

## Elements

A variable or a function value of the type *own* under each type so far: the
type so far after it. `W→L`: the value is converted to the type so far; a
single letter: the value keeps its type, and the type so far becomes it; `Q~ (L)`:
a Quick held with its fraction, the type so far stays Long (#1178). A Byte value
is always extended to a Word in its register; that is no change of type.

| own | – | B | W | L | Q | F |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B | B | B | B→W | B→L | B→Q | B→F |
| W | W | W | W | W→L | W→Q | W→F |
| L | L | L | L | L | L→Q | L→F |
| Q | Q | Q | Q | Q~ (L) | Q | Q→F |
| F | F | F | F | F | F | F |

## Constants

A constant takes the type it is wanted in, or the size it needs; it is written in
that type, without conversion code. The cell is the type so far after it;
"(whole)": a constant written with a point that is taken as the whole number it
is. A negative constant is the constant with a minus before it.

| constant | kind | – | B | W | L | Q | F |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `5` | a whole number of Byte size | B | B | W | L | Q | F |
| `300` | a whole number of Word size | W | W | W | L | Q | F |
| `100000` | a whole number of Long size | L | L | L | L | L | F |
| `1.5` | a fraction that fits a Quick | F | F | F | F | Q | F |
| `40000.5` | a fraction beyond the Quick range | F | F | F | F | F | F |
| `2.0` | a whole value written with a point | F | B (whole) | F | F | Q | F |
| `300.0` | the same of Word size | F | W (whole) | F | F | Q | F |
| `1e10` | a whole part beyond a Long | F | F | F | F | F | F |

Under a Byte type so far (#1188) a constant with a fraction (`1.5`) is a Float,
so the operation is computed in that type and only its result is converted to
the Byte; a whole value written with a point (`2.0`) is made the whole number, a Byte.
A `Data.b` value with a fraction (`Data.b 1.5`) is made the whole number, a Byte.

## The exceptions and their issues

The rules of the original compiler with the port's fixes of these original
bugs; each is described on [The type of an expression in
blitz2](expression-types.md):

* #978: an equality comparison of a byte value with a constant from 128 to 255
  takes the constant as the byte it stands for ([deviations](deviations.md)).
* #1177: the operands of a comparison are compared with their own values
  ([A comparison starts again](expression-types.md#a-comparison-starts-again)).
* #1178: a Quick under a Long type so far keeps its fraction
  ([The port: a Quick keeps its
  fraction](expression-types.md#the-port-a-quick-keeps-its-fraction-1178)).
* #1179: an array index after the first is a Long, as the first
  ([Where this is a problem](expression-types.md#where-this-is-a-problem)).
* #1182: a comparison as the right operand is converted up to the left
  operand's type ([A comparison starts again](expression-types.md#a-comparison-starts-again)).
* #1183 (open): a left operand of a comparison that is itself an operation keeps
  the type so far ([A comparison starts again](expression-types.md#a-comparison-starts-again)).
* #1186, #1188: constants with a point under a Byte type so far ([A constant with
  a fraction under a Byte type so
  far](expression-types.md#a-constant-with-a-fraction-under-a-byte-type-so-far-1188)).
* #1209: `&`, `|`, `AND`, `OR`, `EOR` take a Quick as a whole number ([Bit
  operators under a Quick type so
  far](expression-types.md#bit-operators-under-a-quick-type-so-far-1209)).
